title: Sell Mineral Rights in Marbleton, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Marbleton, WY | Sublette Co
metaDescription: Marbleton, WY mineral owner near the Jonah and Pinedale gas fields in Sublette County? Get a fair cash offer for your interest.
heroLead: Marbleton sits paired with Big Piney at the edge of Sublette County's tight-gas country, close to two of Wyoming's largest gas discoveries of the past thirty years.
intro: The Jonah Field and Pinedale Anticline transformed this corner of the Green River Basin starting in the late 1990s, tight-sand gas out of the Lance and Mesaverde formations developed at a scale that reshaped Sublette County's economy. Marbleton-area minerals sit close enough to that core that many local families have real production history to show for it.

sections.heading: Jonah and Pinedale's tight-gas boom
paragraphs: Operators like Jonah Energy and, historically, Ultra Petroleum, developed this play through dense well spacing on tight Lance and Mesaverde sands, requiring hydraulic fracturing to produce economically. Production peaked in the 2000s and 2010s and has settled into a longer decline phase, but the field remains one of the most significant onshore gas plays in the country.

sections.heading: Marbleton's position relative to the core
paragraphs: Whether your specific tract sits inside the dense core development or on the field's flank makes a real difference in both current production and decline expectations. Core acreage tends to have higher historical volumes and steadier decline; flank acreage may have seen lighter development or none at all.

sections.heading: What a Marbleton-area offer is built on
paragraphs: Current production volume, decline trend, and unit position relative to the Jonah and Pinedale core. Bring your division order and recent check stubs for a producing interest; Sublette County Clerk records in Pinedale can confirm your section's unit status either way.

sections.heading: Marbleton and Big Piney's shared oil identity
paragraphs: Marbleton and neighboring Big Piney function almost as one community for oil and gas history, sharing infrastructure, workforce, and often overlapping unit boundaries from the Jonah and Pinedale development era. If your family holds interests near either town, checking both for lease and unit history is worthwhile.

faqs.question: Is my Marbleton-area interest inside the Jonah or Pinedale core?
faqs.answer: Check your division order or Sublette County Clerk records to confirm your legal description's position relative to the established field boundaries.

faqs.question: How fast does Pinedale-area production decline?
faqs.answer: Tight-gas wells typically show a steep initial decline followed by a long, low-volume tail. That curve is factored into any offer on producing acreage.

faqs.question: Are Jonah and Pinedale still actively drilled today?
faqs.answer: Activity has slowed from its 2000s and 2010s peak as the core has matured, though development and workover activity continues at a reduced pace.

faqs.question: Should I check both Marbleton and Big Piney records for my interest?
faqs.answer: Yes, if your acreage sits near the shared boundary between the two communities. Sublette County Clerk records in Pinedale cover both areas under one office.
